title: After Hours
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Emi, a 24-year-old drifting through an unsatisfying life, is ditched by a friend at a Tokyo nightclub and rescued from unwanted attention by Kei, a confident 30-year-old DJ. They spend the night together, and Emi is drawn into Kei's music world, becoming a VJ for club events as their romance grows over three volumes.
life_message: Finding love and creative work you care about can pull you out of a drifting, unfulfilled life.

content.note: Emi and Kei sleep together on their first night (Wikipedia; ANN); reviewers say not graphic. MangaUpdates LGBT Scenes and Nudity; AniList Nudity 32%.
Adult casual speech; not documented (to verify).
Alcohol throughout club nights and at Kei's home (ANN); no drugs mentioned.
Going home with a stranger met at a club; Emi still lives with a boyfriend (ANN).

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Conflict handled calmly; Kei defuses a drunk rather than fighting (ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Adults choose love and nightlife work freely without family pressure (Wikipedia).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Chosen music community, not family, is Emi's circle.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Club scene and partners treated as peers.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Urban Tokyo nightlife with no religious or traditional frame.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Fulfillment through art and love drives the plot (ANN).

folkways.japan: Shows Tokyo club culture and the 'office drifter' malaise of young Japanese adults, a setting rare in published yuri.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewers call it subdued slice of life and fault it for not exploring Emi's identity, so the message is left implicit.
delivery.note: The romance is presented as ordinary rather than argued for; reviewers note the story avoids discussing sexuality directly.

winners_losers: Emi and Kei find love and purpose; no one is cast as an opponent; sympathy goes to the couple.
to_verify: Explicitness of the sex and nudity in later volumes.
